The Other Courses.name: The Other Courses
The Other Courses.description:
📚 The Hero Course gets the cameras. Everyone else studies, builds and plans what keeps heroes running.

📍 U.A. main building lobby · first morning
🎭 Grounded, funny, ambitious
👥 For General Studies, Support Course and Management Course students
The Other Courses.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy, the day after move-in at Heights Alliance. The PC is a first-year in General Studies (Classes 1-C to 1-E), the Support Course (1-F to 1-H) or the Management Course (1-I to 1-K), as their Path states. Homeroom starts at 8:30. General Studies runs a full academic program, and many in it sat the Hero Course exam and failed; U.A.'s rule lets a General Studies student with strong results move into the Hero Course, and a weak Hero Course student out. Support students design, build and repair gear and costumes in Power Loader's Development Studio. Management students learn agency finance, contracts, public relations and the press. All Might joined the faculty this spring, so reporters wait at the gate and the whole buzzing campus talks about him. Nothing has happened yet this year.

THE PLACE: The Main Building Lobby: the sunlit ground floor where the two long wings of the H-shaped glass building meet. A bright, high hall with corridors to the first-year homerooms, the Faculty Office, the Infirmary and the clanking Development Studio, the fragrant doors of Lunch Rush's Cafeteria and elevators to the upper years; every door is oversized for students of any size. At this hour it is filling for the first time this year, and ceiling speakers carry the clear chime.

THE MOMENT: A loud knot of Hero Course first-years stops dead in the middle of the hall to argue over which corridor leads to 1-A, blocking everyone. A Support first-year's rattling cart of parts clips the knot, a steel bolt rolls across the tile to the PC's feet, and from the Development Studio corridor comes a bang and a rolling puff of gray smoke.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Hitoshi Shinso: Class 1-C; low and dry, quietly measuring every Hero Course student who walks past.
- Mei Hatsume: Class 1-H; the oil-smudged source of the smoke, darting back out for more parts.
- Power Loader: shouts "Hatsume!" from the studio door; he teaches the Support Course and signs off on every test.
- Present Mic: teaches English and greets the packed lobby at broadcast volume on his way through.
- Hound Dog: the guidance counselor; students who scuffle or break rules end up in front of him.
- Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, Nejire Hado: the Big Three cut through between lectures; Nejire cheerily asks strangers whatever she is wondering, Mirio jokes, Tamaki finds a wall to face.
- Lunch Rush: propping open the cafeteria doors as the smell of fresh broth drifts out.
- Tenya Iida, Katsuki Bakugo, Neito Monoma: Hero Course first-years crossing the hall; Iida directs traffic unasked, Bakugo shoves with a snarl, Monoma performs.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. General Studies: Shinso, beside the PC, watches the Hero Course knot and says something dry about who got in; the notice about course transfers is pinned to the board above them.
- U.A. Support Course: the bolt belongs to the cart; Mei pops out of the smoke wanting it back and wanting to know the PC's Quirk, with Power Loader's shout right behind her.
- U.A. Management Course: a rattled Hero Course first-year who was photographed at the gate this morning asks the nearest Management student what to say to the press, and Nejire Hado stops to listen with open curiosity.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: someone in the Hero Course knot says, loud enough to carry, that the other courses are for people who did not make it; Shinso hears it too.
- Family Business: Lunch Rush is one pair of hands short at the cafeteria doors, and the PC has worked a busy counter before.
- Default: the PC is nearest the knot when the smoke reaches it, the argument turns to coughing, and the crowd starts to push.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in the Main Building Lobby until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; Quirk use outside supervised class or training is a rule break.
- The other courses matter: their work, grades and ambitions carry the same weight as the Hero Course's.
- Nothing of the year has happened yet; no festival, transfer, test or attack is promised or foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after today each course settles into its own routine. General Studies: a full academic load in the General Studies Classrooms (mathematics, sciences, literature, English, history) that runs into the afternoon, homework, clubs, and supervised physical education, where a Quirk is lawful. Support: morning lectures in the Support Course Classrooms, then long, loud afternoons and evenings in the Development Studio, where nothing is tested without Power Loader's sign-off and Hero Course students bring broken gear with deadlines. Management: the Management Course Classrooms, tables in a horseshoe under wall screens flashing hero rankings and merchandise sales, case studies, group pitches and graded presentations. Everyone shares Lunch Rush's bustling Cafeteria at lunch and the Other Course Dorm Halls at night, all three courses mixed on every floor, with a curfew.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Hitoshi Shinso: says little, answers a question with a question, and measures whether a newcomer looks down on General Studies.
- Mei Hatsume: asks about a Quirk before a name, sees every stranger as a test pilot or a client, and pitches her babies mid-sentence.
- Power Loader: tired, patient and technical; explains a failure by its cause and signs off only on a safe test.
- Hound Dog: stern and short, until anger turns his words into barking growls.
- Hero Course first-years treat the other courses by temperament, not by course: Tenya Iida is formally courteous to everyone, Katsuki Bakugo is rude to everyone, and Neito Monoma counts any audience as his.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: pick up the bolt and return it or keep it, follow the smoke to the Development Studio, push through the knot or go around it, read the notice board, answer Shinso or ask him something back, help with the cart, or head for their own wing before the chime. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The opening needs no fight: a returned bolt, a cleared hallway or a first word with Shinso or Mei completes the scene.
- In their own field the other courses are the experts: a Support student out-builds the Hero Course, and a Management student out-reads the press.
The Other Courses.firstQuest: Make a name at U.A. on a path the cameras ignore: study, build or plan something the Hero Course cannot do without.
The Other Courses.questGenerationGuidance: Favor each course's work. General Studies: lectures, exams, being overlooked, Shinso's drive, and what earning a transfer takes. Support: build requests, failed tests, Power Loader's inspections, Mei Hatsume's chaos, Hero Course clients and test pilots, safety rules, and sponsors noticing good gear. Management: agency case studies, budgets, contracts, All Might's press frenzy, a Hero Course student's public image, mock negotiations. Shared campus life: cafeteria lines, library, dorm halls, the Big Three as mentors or puzzles, Hound Dog's office after a scuffle. Public events like the Sports Festival arrive only as the story reaches them, with open outcomes. Stakes: grades, standing, a rival's respect, a project succeeding or failing. Hero Course students enter as clients, test pilots, rivals or friends; the PC's coursework stays central.
